## Reaching rustygate

dialoghelper calls rustygate’s API through a `rustygate` comm in a
gateway kernel, without a URL or token. Explicit HTTP clients can use
`RUSTYGATE_URL`.
[`CommTransport`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#commtransport)
lets jupyasyncclient’s clients use the same routes over the comm.
[`_rg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#_rg) calls
the few private routes dialoghelper needs, such as `caller` and `run`.

The `comm_open` carries the route, method and headers, with the request
body in its first buffer. rustygate replies with a `comm_msg` holding
the status and headers, then sends each piece of the body in further
messages, and closes the comm when the body ends. Closing the comm from
the kernel cancels the request, which stops a streaming prompt.
rustygate adds the id of the execute that opened the comm, so it can
tell which cell made the request.

[`browser`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#browser)
runs JavaScript in each browser showing this dialog. It opens a
[`browser`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#browser)
comm, and Solveit runs the code in every connected browser as the body
of an async function. That function receives `done`, which answers the
call, and `rid`, the call’s id. Code that answers later from an event
handler can instead pass `rid` on and call `pushData(rid, {result})`, as
the solveit-chrome extension does.

The first browser to answer supplies the result. A JavaScript error
raises `RuntimeError`, and no answer within `timeout` seconds raises
`TimeoutError`. With `wait=False`,
[`browser`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#browser)
returns at once. The code never appears in a cell’s output, so reloading
a page doesn’t run it again.

[`add_html`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#add_html)
swaps the `hx-swap-oob` elements of some HTML into each browser’s page.
It runs `htmx.swap` through
[`browser`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#browser),
and returns without waiting:

``` python
add_html(Div(P('Hi'), hx_swap_oob='beforeend:#dialog-container'))
```

    {'success': 'Content added to DOM'}

[`realpath()`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#realpath)
returns the gateway’s on-disk root. `realpath('')` returns the current
notebook’s folder. Other relative paths use that folder, regardless of
the kernel’s cwd. A leading slash uses the gateway root. Targets need
not exist. `..` can move up within the root, and a path that resolves
outside it raises `ValueError`.
[`realpath`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#realpath)
makes no gateway call and doesn’t need awaiting, so a `$` reference can
use it.

These helpers resolve names against `dh_settings['path']`, the kernel’s
notebook, which follows renames. An unbound kernel can resolve
root-qualified paths but has no notebook-relative base.
[`list_dialogs()`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#list_dialogs)
lists the current notebook’s folder by default and keeps the existing
notebook-extension and folder-suffix conventions.

### data_root

``` python
def data_root():
```

*The gateway root recorded at startup, or derived from the current
notebook’s folder*

The editing tools use the gateway’s cells API. They send batches of
operations to add or delete cells, merge metadata, or toggle flags. An
edit that needs a message’s existing content reads that cell before
sending its replacement.

Writes do not check whether the cell changed since the read. The last
write to a field wins, as it did with direct file editing. Solveit
updates its view from the gateway’s broadcasts rather than waiting for a
file watcher to report a diff.

[`cells_client`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#cells_client)
binds a client to one dialog’s notebook, using the comm proxy in a
gateway kernel. The kernel’s bootstrap records the gateway root in
`dh_settings['root']`, and
[`data_root`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#data_root)
returns it for operations that use filesystem paths. Outside a dialog,
[`data_root`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#data_root)
is the current directory.

### read_msg

``` python
async def read_msg(
    n:int=-1, # Message index (if relative, +ve is downwards)
    relative:bool=True, # Is `n` relative to current message (True) or absolute (False)?
    id:str=None, # Message id to find (defaults to current message)
    start_line:int=1, # Starting line to view
    end_line:int=None, # End line (defaults to last line if None; -1 for EOF)
    nums:bool=False, # Whether to show line numbers
    lnhashs:bool=False, # Show exhash `lineno|hash|` addresses instead of line numbers?
    dname:str='', # Dialog to get info for; defaults to current dialog
)->dict | None:
```

*Get the message indexed in the current dialog, or None when there’s no
such message.* NB: Messages in the current dialog above the current
message are *already* visible; use this only when you need line numbers
for editing operations, or for messages not in the current dialog or
below the current message. - To get the exact message use `n=0` and
`relative=True` together with `id`. - To get a relative message use `n`
(relative position index). - To get the nth message use `n` with
`relative=False`, e.g `n=0` first message, `n=-1` last message.

### find_msgs

``` python
async def find_msgs(
    re_pattern:str='', # Optional regex to search for (re.DOTALL+re.MULTILINE is used)
    msg_type:str=None, # optional limit by message type ('code', 'note', or 'prompt')
    before:int=0, # Include additional n msgs before matches
    after:int=0, # Include additional n msgs after matches
    context:int=None, # Include additional n msgs around matches (default 1, or 0 when `headers_only`)
    use_case:bool=False, # Use case-sensitive matching?
    use_regex:bool=True, # Use regex matching?
    only_err:bool=None, # Only messages with errors if True, only those without if False, all if None
    only_exp:bool=None, # Only exported messages if True, only unexported if False, all if None
    only_chg:bool=False, # Only messages whose input differs from Git HEAD
    ids:str='', # Optionally filter by comma-separated list of message ids
    limit:int=None, # Optionally limit number of returned items
    include_output:bool=True, # Include output in returned dict?
    include_meta:bool=True, # Include all additional message metadata
    as_xml:bool=False, # Use concise unescaped XML output format
    nums:bool=False, # Show line numbers?
    trunc_out:bool=False, # Middle-out truncate code output to 100 characters?
    trunc_in:bool=False, # Middle-out truncate cell content to 80 characters?
    headers_only:bool=False, # Only return note messages that are headers (first line only); cannot be used together with `header_section`
    header_section:str=None, # Find section starting with this header; returns it plus all children
    include_skipped:bool=False, # Include messages hidden from AI (skipped)?
    dname:str='', # Dialog to get info for; defaults to current dialog
)->list[dict]: # Messages in requested dialog that contain the given information
```

*Often it is more efficient to call
[`view_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#view_dlg)
(not
[`find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#find_msgs))
to see the whole dialog, so you can use it all from then on.* Message
ids are identical to those in LLM chat history, so do NOT call this to
view a specific message if it’s in the chat history–instead use
[`view_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#view_msg).
Do NOT use find_msgs to view message content in the current dialog above
the current prompt – these are *already* provided in LLM context, so
just read the content there directly. (NB: LLM context only includes
messages *above* the current prompt, whereas
[`find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#find_msgs)
can access *all* messages.) To refer to a found message from code, use
its `id` field.

``` python
1+1
```

    2

``` python
r = await find_msgs(r'1\+1', include_meta=False, include_output=True, context=0)
```

### add_msg

``` python
async def add_msg(
    content:str, # Content of the message (i.e the message prompt, code, or note text)
    msg_type:str='note', # Message type, can be 'code', 'note', or 'prompt'
    msgid:str=None, # Message to place the new one beside; default: the calling cell in its own dialog, else the end (or start for `position='before'`)
    position:str='after', # 'after' or 'before' `msgid`, or the dialog's 'start' or 'end'
    dname:str='', # Dialog to add to; defaults to current dialog
    output:str='', # Prompt/code output; Code outputs must be .ipynb-compatible JSON array
    exported:int=0, # Mark message as exported (stored as nbdev `export` metadata)?
    skipped:int=0, # Hide message from prompt?
    i_collapsed:int=0, # Collapse input?
    o_collapsed:int=0, # Collapse output?
    heading_collapsed:int=0, # Collapse heading section?
    pinned:int=0, # Pin to context?
    bookmark:int=0, # Bookmark number, 1 to 9, or 0 for none
)->str: # Message ID of newly created message
```

*Add a message to a dialog, returning its id*

Without `msgid`,
[`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#add_msg)
places the new message after the calling cell: the cell whose code is
running, or the prompt whose tool call is running. `position='before'`
places it before that cell instead. Successive calls therefore come out
in reverse order. To add a run of messages in order, pass each returned
id as the next call’s `msgid`. When there’s no calling cell, or the
message goes to another dialog, it goes at the end, or at the start for
`position='before'`. `position='start'` and `position='end'` put it at
the dialog’s start or end, whatever the calling cell. The id of the
prompt a model is answering is the `sid` attribute of its `<prompt>`
tag.

``` python
_id = await add_msg('testing')
_id
```

    '9ed1250c'

``` python
async def read_msgid(
    id:str, # Message id to find
    start_line:int=1, # Starting line to view
    end_line:int=None, # End line (defaults to last line if None; -1 for EOF)
    nums:bool=False, # Whether to show line numbers

    dname:str='', # Dialog to get message from; defaults to current dialog

)->dict | None:
```

*Get message `id`, or None when there’s no such message. Message IDs can
be view directly in LLM chat history/context, or found in
[`find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#find_msgs)
results.* Use `add_to_dlg` if the LLM or human may need to refer to the
message content again later.

``` python
r = await read_msg(-2)
print((await read_msg(-2)).content)
```

    _id = await add_msg('testing')
    _id

[`read_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#read_msg)
returns a `dict2obj` result. Access its fields as dictionary keys, such
as `r['content']`, or attributes, such as `r.content`. Functions that
take message ids also accept the DOM form that Solveit’s page and
message links use, with a leading `_`, such as `_f5fd1d54`.

``` python
bmsg = await add_msg('just below the calling cell')
emsg = await add_msg('at the end', position='end')
```

``` python
test_eq((await read_msg(-1))['id'], bmsg)
test_eq((await read_msg(-1, relative=False))['id'], emsg)
test_eq((await read_msgid('_'+bmsg))['id'], bmsg)
```

### update_msg

``` python
async def update_msg(
    id:str=None, # id of message to update (if None, uses current message)
    msg:Optional[Dict]=None, # Dictionary of field keys/values to update
    dname:str='', # Dialog to get info for; defaults to current dialog
    log_changed:bool=False, # Add a note showing the diff?
    *, content:str | None=None, # Content of the message (i.e the message prompt, code, or note text)
    msg_type:str | None=None, # Message type, can be 'code', 'note', or 'prompt'
    output:str | None=None, # Prompt/code output; Code outputs must be .ipynb-compatible JSON array
    exported:int | None=None, # Set export state (nbdev `export` metadata)?
    skipped:int | None=None, # Hide message from prompt?
    i_collapsed:int | None=None, # Collapse input?
    o_collapsed:int | None=None, # Collapse output?
    heading_collapsed:int | None=None, # Collapse heading section?
    pinned:int | None=None, # Pin to context?
    meta:dict | None=None, # Replace message meta wholesale
    mergemeta:dict | None=None, # Deep-merge into message meta; a `None` value deletes its key
)->str:
```

*Update an existing message. Provide either `msg` OR field key/values to
update.* - Use `content` param to update contents. - Only include
parameters to update–missing ones will be left unchanged.

``` python
_id = await add_msg('testing')
```

``` python
_id = await update_msg(_id, content='toasting')
```

``` python
_id = await update_msg(_id, skipped=1)
```

[`update_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#update_msg)
follows `Message.update` for metadata. `meta=` replaces the metadata
dictionary. `mergemeta=` merges nested dictionaries and deletes keys
whose value is `None`.

A metadata merge on its own uses a gateway `merge` operation. It follows
JSON merge-patch rules, where `null` deletes a key. A metadata
replacement, or a merge combined with content changes, uses the
serialized message in an unconditional `update` operation.

``` python
await update_msg(_id, mergemeta=dict(pins=dict(a=1)))
test_eq((await read_msgid(_id))['meta']['pins'], {'a': 1})
await update_msg(_id, mergemeta=dict(pins=None))
assert 'pins' not in (await read_msgid(_id))['meta']
```

``` python
msg = await read_msgid(_id)
msg['content'] = 'toasted'
await update_msg(msg=msg)
```

    'e49c9729'

``` python
await del_msgs(_id)
```

    ['e49c9729']

``` python

    position:str='after', # 'after' or 'before' `msgid`, or the dialog's 'start' or 'end'

```

*Paste the gateway clipboard’s messages where
[`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#add_msg)
would place a new one, returning their ids*

[`paste_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#paste_msgs)
places the pasted messages where
[`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#add_msg)
would place a new one. These functions use the gateway’s clipboard,
which Solveit’s copy and paste use too, so messages copied in the
browser can be pasted from code and the other way round. A copy replaces
the clipboard’s contents. The first paste after a cut keeps the cut
messages’ ids, so links to them keep working. Every other paste gives
the copies new ids.

### Dlg conveniences

These functions manage dialogs and their kernels through rustygate.
[`create_or_run_dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#create_or_run_dialog)
gets or starts the kernel bound to a dialog, creating the dialog if it’s
missing. A new dialog starts with its folder’s `TEMPLATE.ipynb` cells
and settings. When the templates set no mode, it takes the current
dialog’s mode.
[`restart_dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#restart_dialog)
keeps the kernel’s id, and
[`rm_dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#rm_dialog)
stops the kernel before deleting the file.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/dialoghelper/blob/main/dialoghelper/core.py#L629"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### run_code_interactive

``` python
async def run_code_interactive(
    code:str, # Code to have user run
):
```

*Insert code into user’s dialog and request for the user to run it. Use
other functions where possible,* but if they can not find needed
information, *ALWAYS* use this instead of guessing or giving up.
IMPORTANT: This tool is TERMINAL - after calling it, you MUST stop all
tool usage and wait for user response. Never call additional tools after
this one.

[`run_cells`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#run_cells)
runs code cells in a dialog’s kernel through rustygate’s run route: the
current dialog’s kernel, unless you pass another dialog’s kernel id.
Rustygate saves each cell’s outputs in the cell and sends them to every
connected client, as for a run started in Solveit, and
[`run_cells`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#run_cells)
returns them. aidialog’s `Message.execute` and `Dialog.execute` differ:
they run messages in a temporary in-process shell.

A tool can call
[`run_cells`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#run_cells)
while its own message is still running. Rustygate runs the requested
cells in a subshell, so they don’t wait behind the calling message in
the main shell’s queue.

When `py` runs with safepyrun’s audit checks, the nested execution
remains inside that audit window.
[`run_cells`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#run_cells)
does not add a separate sandbox.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/dialoghelper/blob/main/dialoghelper/core.py#L671"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
)->list: # Each cell's saved outputs
```

*Run code cells in a dialog’s kernel through rustygate, saving their
outputs; the run stops at the first cell that raises*

## Prompts

[`run_prompt`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#run_prompt)
asks rustygate to run a prompt. With a prompt message’s `msgid`,
rustygate answers that prompt with the cells above it as context and
saves the reply in the message, as when a user runs it in Solveit. With
`text`, rustygate answers a prompt that isn’t in the dialog, using the
cells up to `msgid` as context, and saves nothing. Without `msgid`, that
context ends at the calling cell.

The reply streams back over the comm, and
[`run_prompt`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#run_prompt)
prints it as it arrives unless `show=False`. It returns the reply in the
format Solveit stores, with each tool call as a fenced block.
Interrupting the cell closes the comm, which cancels the turn, and a
prompt message keeps its partial reply. A prompt run from code doesn’t
wait in the kernel’s queue. `tools` names the tools the model may call:
functions in the kernel’s namespace, or rustygate’s own `exec` and
`spawn_agent`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/dialoghelper/blob/main/dialoghelper/core.py#L737"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### run_prompt

``` python
async def run_prompt(
    msgid:str=None, # Prompt message to run; with `text`, the message the context ends at (default: the calling cell)
    text:str=None, # Prompt text to answer without saving anything in the dialog
    tools:list=None, # Names of the tools the model may call
    show:bool=True, # Print the reply as it streams?
    kid:str=None, # Kernel whose dialog holds the prompt (default: this one); with `text` and another dialog's kernel, pass `msgid`
)->str: # The reply, in its stored format
```

*Run a prompt message, or answer `text` with the dialog as context, and
return the reply*

``` python
pid = await add_msg('Reply with just the word: hello', msg_type='prompt')
reply = await run_prompt(pid)
```

``` python
test_eq((await read_msgid(pid))['output'], reply)
await del_msgs(pid)
```

    ['a3c96594']

``` python
await run_prompt(text='What is 2+2? Reply with just the number.')
```
